g1-implement.title: verify + close primitives: implement
g1-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g1. THREE functions in scripts/spine_lifecycle.py:

(a) done_refusal(spine, *, tree_clean, episodes_captured) -> str|None -- PURE, ONE refusal string or None, covering ONLY the two genuinely new checks (tree clean/staged, episodes captured). REWORK NOTE (PLAN_CRITIC/PLAN_CRITIQUE finding 1, confirmed against checklist_engine.py -- if a prior attempt's done_refusal delegates to closeout_refusal for terminality/lease/archive-exists, that is the bug to fix, not a shape to keep): do NOT call or fold in closeout_refusal here. The lease is BY DEFINITION still active when this runs -- before _advance_and_release -- so a done_refusal that includes closeout_refusal's lease check (`status != 'released'`) refuses on every legitimate invocation, before the function that would actually release it ever runs. Gate-terminality is verified downstream by advance's own postcondition refusal; lease/terminality/archive-exists is verified exactly once, AFTER release, by close_work's existing unmodified closeout_refusal call -- never duplicated here.

(b) _engine_call(argv) -> tuple[str, int] -- the SINGLE choke point for every in-process checklist_engine.main(argv) call in this module, mirroring the exact pattern scripts/mcp_spine_server.py's existing pass-through tools already use (its module docstring: 'Every tool builds an argv and calls checklist_engine.main(argv), capturing stdout, stderr and the exit code'). It MUST catch BOTH checklist_engine.EngineError AND SystemExit: argparse calls sys.exit(2) on an unparseable argv and checklist_engine.main()'s own try/except catches only EngineError, so an argv-shape mismatch (a typo, or lane A's concurrent rewrite changing a flag) would otherwise escape as SystemExit instead of the captured (output, exit_code) pair every caller here assumes. Returns always; never raises. [PLAN_CRITIC finding 4]

(c) _advance_and_release(spine_path, session_id, *, root, why=None) -> dict -- impure, via _engine_call only. If the terminal gate is 'pending', 'start' it; if it is not yet terminal, 'advance' it passing --why <why> when a why was supplied and --mechanical otherwise; then 'release --session-id <session_id>'.

LOAD-BEARING (PLAN_CRITIC finding 1, independently verified by the Commander against checklist_engine.py:2519-2534 in advance() and _run_verb:3361-3370): advance()'s require_why parameter is computed LIVE at the CLI boundary from _trip_hard_band_reading(...), NOT from any flag the caller passes -- and when it is true the engine REFUSES --mechanical outright ('context is at/over the hard limit, so this gate cannot be closed silently'). So never assume --mechanical works. When the advance half refuses for ANY reason, return that refusal text VERBATIM as the one actionable refusal (the engine's own message already names the fix) and do NOT attempt the release.

Tests in tests/test_spine_lifecycle.py: (1) fixture spine at its terminal gate, not yet advanced -> released afterwards; (2) fixture spine with an unmet postcondition -> refusal text passes through unchanged AND engine_session.status is still 'active' (release never attempted); (3) THE HARD-BAND PATH -- write a gauge file at/over the hard band beside a fixture spine (gauge_reader.gauge_filename(owner)/GAUGE_FILENAME shape, fill_fraction high enough to trip), assert a why-less finish attempt returns the engine's why-required refusal instead of silently closing, then assert the SAME fixture closes cleanly once a why is supplied; (4) _engine_call returns a non-zero exit code rather than raising SystemExit on a deliberately malformed argv.

g2-implement.title: reap + child-plan release: implement
g2-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g2. TWO functions in scripts/spine_lifecycle.py:

(a) force_reap(project_dir) -> dict|None -- a library call into spine_rail's existing _binding_transaction(project_dir, lambda reaped: reaped) (import scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py via spine_lifecycle.py's own sys.path insert, same pattern as its other imports; ZERO edits to spine_rail.py), forcing an immediate persist of the already-reaped map instead of waiting on some future unrelated session's touch.

(b) _release_child_plans(spine_path, work_dir, *, root, reason) -> dict with keys {released: list[str], unclaimed_active: list[str]}.

THREE safety properties, each a SHIPPED RUNTIME GUARD and not a test-only discipline (PLAN_CRITIC finding 3, independently verified by the Commander against checklist_engine.py:1133-1147 release() and :975-1005 require_session()):

  1. LINEAGE, NOT DIRECTORY PROXIMITY. A child plan is identified STRUCTURALLY: a JSON file whose realpath is strictly inside work_dir AND which some task in the parent spine names in its child_checklist field (resolve each task's child_checklist relative to work_dir). An active-leased JSON under work_dir that NO task claims as its child_checklist is LEFT ALONE and reported in unclaimed_active -- never silently released. 'Any active JSON under work_dir' is explicitly the wrong predicate: it would seize a lease a different, still-working agent genuinely holds.

  2. HONEST NON-OWNER RELEASE. Do NOT read a child's own engine_session.session_id and hand it back to release() as the caller id -- release()'s ownership check is `session_id != sess.get('session_id')`, so that makes the check TAUTOLOGICAL and forges ownership this run does not have. Release each child as the explicit non-owner it is: 'release --force --reason <reason naming the parent work_id and that this is a parent closeout>', which the engine records as a forced non-owner release and so leaves a real audit trail.

  3. ESCAPE REFUSAL. Resolve every candidate with realpath and refuse any whose resolved path is not strictly inside work_dir, so a symlink cannot reach a spine outside the work area.

Tests: force_reap fixture (binding-store entry whose target is already released -> gone immediately, asserted via spine_rail.load_binding, not by waiting for another transaction); _release_child_plans with 0/1/2 children DECLARED via child_checklist; NEGATIVE -- a spine outside work_dir sharing the work_id prefix is never touched; NEGATIVE -- an active-leased JSON inside work_dir that no task declares is not released and IS reported in unclaimed_active; NEGATIVE -- a symlink inside work_dir pointing outside it is refused.

g3-implement.title: finish_work composition + dispose + CLI: implement
g3-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g3: add finish_work(spine_path, *, root, session_id, today, why=None, push=True, open_pr=False) -> dict to scripts/spine_lifecycle.py, composing g1+g2's functions.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING (PLAN_CRITIC finding 2, verified by the Commander against spine_rail.py:311-366 _reap_binding_entries):
  1. done_refusal on the current state -- refuse-and-stop, ONE actionable message, zero mutation on failure.
  2. _release_child_plans FIRST -- before any reap.
  3. _advance_and_release on the top-level spine -- so the top spine's own release is the LAST journaled action on that spine (the lease covers every journaled action on it).
  4. force_reap -- AFTER every release, never before. _reap_binding_entries only drops an entry whose target reads engine_session.status == 'released', so reaping first leaves every still-active child's binding entry behind for a future incidental transaction -- reproducing the exact #552 staleness this run exists to end.
  5. close_work (existing, UNMODIFIED) -- the archive move.
  6. git push when push=True.
  7. open_pr(...) ONLY when open_pr=True.

open_pr is a NEW independently-callable helper NOT invoked by default, per the floated PR-opening question (decision:pr-opening-question-is-not-yours): a wrapper script can call spine_lifecycle.open_pr(...) itself today, and finish_work(open_pr=True) is the only change needed if the engine verb is later ruled to own it -- neither ruling costs rework.

REFUSAL SHAPE (PLAN_CRITIC finding 6): finish_work never raises for a closeout refusal. It returns {ok: False, refusal: <verbatim engine or done_refusal text>, stage: <which step refused>} and performs no further step; on success it returns {ok: True, work_id, branch, head, archive, pushed, pr, child_plans_released, unclaimed_active}. SpineLifecycleError stays reserved for genuine faults, not for a refusal that is a normal outcome.

Add scripts/spine_done_cli.py (NEW file, not fenced) -- a thin CLI over finish_work (--file, --root, --session-id, --today, --why, --no-push, --open-pr) printing the returned dict as JSON and exiting non-zero on a refusal. This is the reachable-today 'one door verb', usable without waiting on lane A's mcp_spine_server.py rewrite.

Add the #552 LEASE-PROOF end-to-end fixture test: build a fixture work area under tmp_path with a top-level spine AND a nested child plan declared via child_checklist, claim BOTH, drive both to their terminal gate, run the structural active-lease census BEFORE (expect 2 active), run finish_work, run the census AFTER (expect 0 active), and assert the archive contains the child. Fixtures under tmp_path only -- never a live spine.

Also write to notes-g.md a READ-ONLY re-measurement of the launch order's lease census (every *.json under .agent-work/ whose engine_session.status is 'active', bucketed by age) against today's base commit, updating the abad896d/2026-08-10 figure of 43.
